features.description: Specify the first desktop workspace, terminal, draft recovery and NOLF integration slice.
acceptance_criteria: Carry forward macOS/Windows, empty-to-split layout, movable tabs, basic editing/optional Vim, persistent sidecar sessions, the session browser and multiple project/worktree roots with explicit per-session bindings as confirmed requirements.

Pin the owner-selected flat NOLF host build/profile; specify actual rendered output/input in a new tab, native host ownership and acceptance commands on both platforms, with VtMB as the second adapter.

Specify stable root identities and local recovery drafts with explicit file saves; define checkpoint/conflict handling, initial Vim subset and predeclared measurable terminal/editor/game budgets; keep agent installers, Quest and XR as later gates.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/032-desktop-v0.md

features.description: Qualify the desktop UI, terminal and game-surface stack on macOS and Windows.
acceptance_criteria: Compare a small set of existing layout/editor/terminal components against native desktop and later Quest-client constraints with source/license/version references.
On both platforms demonstrate a real PTY, editable text/Vim-mode feasibility and a real cooperative graphical surface with resize/input; static mockups are insufficient.
Measure agreed budgets and choose an implementation stack with known limits and rollback; failure produces a revised proposal, not a supported-platform claim.
features.deliverable: docs/decisions/desktop-stack.md and bounded feasibility prototype

features.description: Implement the empty workspace with recursive splits and movable tab groups.
acceptance_criteria: Start empty, split horizontally/vertically, resize and collapse splits, and open/reorder/move tabs between pane groups.
Keyboard/pointer focus follows the intended tab; moving a view preserves its session and root binding and does not trigger a new session or change another tab's context.
Exercise the actual UI on macOS and Windows, including minimum sizes and displays with different scaling.
features.deliverable: orchestrator layout implementation and UI evidence

features.description: Implement a desktop sidecar that owns interactive sessions independently of views.
acceptance_criteria: Session records identify owning sidecar, stable project/worktree root, type, target, launch cwd, process/PTY identity and state; launch only through explicit commands and distinguish shell cwd from launch association.
Closing a view or GUI leaves sessions alive; reconnect attaches to the same session; explicit Stop terminates the intended process tree and reports exit.

Test sessions in two separate worktrees, GUI loss, sidecar failure, missing roots and stale identities on macOS/Windows; never retarget a session by focus/display name or claim a terminated process has resumed.
features.deliverable: sidecar session service and lifecycle tests

features.description: Connect real terminal panes to sidecar-owned PTY sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise an interactive shell/full-screen terminal program with input, resize, scrollback, Unicode, paste and control keys on both desktops.

Move/detach/reattach terminals bound to different roots without losing their process and retained output; focus routes input only to the selected session and a shell cwd change does not rebind its launch root.
Long-lived sessions have no inherited verification-job deadline; measure responsiveness and retain failure/exit state.
features.deliverable: terminal provider and desktop acceptance evidence

features.description: Provide project tree, previews and basic text editing with optional Vim mode.
acceptance_criteria: Browse multiple declared roots, preview files, and edit/save text with undo/redo/search, dirty-buffer status and external-change handling; identical relative filenames in separate worktrees retain distinct root-bound buffers and save destinations.
Exercise the F32-defined Vim subset and ordinary editing on macOS/Windows; preserve supported encoding/line endings and avoid silent overwrite of external edits.

Retain unsaved edits as local recovery drafts on view close/GUI restart and write working files only on explicit Save; exercise external edits, checkpoint failure and explicit Discard without losing the only unsaved copy; large/binary/unsupported files fail or preview explicitly.
features.deliverable: file/tree/editor providers and edit-path evidence

features.description: Persist layout and recover views onto retained sessions after GUI restart.
acceptance_criteria: Restore splits, tab placement, stable root/session associations and durable local editor drafts after closing/reopening the GUI with multiple projects/worktrees; no restore path silently writes working files.
Resolve live session IDs through the sidecar; no restore path relaunches commands automatically or confuses a dead process with a live one.

Interrupted saves and unknown persistence versions recover with an actionable result; test macOS/Windows paths and changed/missing/removed roots without silently remapping sessions, relaunching commands or stopping retained processes.
features.deliverable: versioned workspace persistence and recovery evidence

features.description: Implement the terminal-based Bash agent selector and extensible launch registry.
acceptance_criteria: Discover supported installed CLI agents and allow an explicit custom installed command; launch in the chosen terminal's explicit root and launch directory regardless of another tab's focused project.
Keep recipes/version detection outside pane code and specify the Windows Bash/native-or-WSL path contract without guessing conversions.
Prove selection/launch both inside the orchestrator and standalone on macOS/Windows, including missing agent and cancelled selection.
features.deliverable: standalone agent launcher and registered CLI recipes

features.description: Add visible selected-agent installation and recoverable setup recipes.
acceptance_criteria: For a user-selected supported recipe, show official source, version, destination and required changes before installation; do not install on tab open alone.
Verify the installed CLI/version and support cancellation, failed download/install and repeat invocation without corrupting an existing installation.
Exercise at least the first agreed real CLI recipe per desktop platform plus isolated failure fixtures; preserve unrelated agent configuration.
features.deliverable: versioned agent install recipes and installation evidence

features.description: Bootstrap project MCP integrations through agent-specific configuration adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Merge the explicitly bound root's project profile through the supported CLI/version adapter without replacing unrelated settings, using a global active project or assuming every agent shares a format.
Distinguish configured, reachable, unsupported and failed integrations; re-running setup is idempotent and exposes repair steps.
Prove the selected agent calls an actual local test MCP tool scoped to its project/session; unknown CLI configuration is not silently guessed.
features.deliverable: agent integration profiles and connectivity evidence

features.description: Implement the cooperative game surface and input contract for desktop panes.
acceptance_criteria: Transport actual frames from a separate graphical process to a tab with explicit session identity, frame lifetime, resize and input semantics.
Prove focus/aspect/DPI handling, view movement, detach/reattach and explicit stop without affecting another session on macOS and Windows.
Measure the F32/F33 budgets and keep the transport distinct from MCP control; expose capabilities suitable for a later remote client.
features.deliverable: versioned surface adapter and native graphical fixture

features.description: Render flat NOLF into an orchestrator tab on macOS and Windows.
acceptance_criteria: From the owning nolf-improved workspace, implement the flat NOLF adapter using the F32-pinned native build/launch profile and user-owned assets.
Show actual game output in a new tab and verify resize, input, tab move, close/reattach and explicit stop through the sidecar on macOS and Windows.
Run relevant existing host gates, record the tested game/profile and rollback; an external window or log-only tab does not complete the pane requirement.
features.deliverable: reLith-owned surface adapter and two-platform game evidence

features.description: Complete the first desktop workflow with a terminal, editor, session browser and flat game tab.
acceptance_criteria: On macOS and Windows execute the empty-to-split workflow with multiple roots, ordinary and optional Vim editing, local draft recovery with explicit saves, real terminals and flat NOLF in a new tab.

Move and detach views, find retained sessions in the browser, reattach after GUI restart, and explicitly stop the intended game/process; identical filenames and similarly named sessions across roots never redirect a file write or session operation.
Record real rendered/input evidence and agreed performance measurements; a layout mock, terminal-only shell or external game window cannot close this milestone.
features.deliverable: docs/evidence/desktop-v0.md and packaged desktop builds

features.description: Provide the session browser for inspecting, reattaching and explicitly stopping sessions.
acceptance_criteria: List live/detached/exited sessions with explicit project/worktree root, type, target, state and attached-view information; distinguish similarly named sessions and retain root association even after its removal from the layout.
Attach or focus an existing session and explicitly stop one with accurate exit reporting; moving/closing the browser does not stop other sessions.

Exercise detached game and terminal sessions across GUI restart on macOS and Windows, including a stale/dead session and two similarly named worktrees; attach and Stop affect only the selected root/session.
features.deliverable: session browser UI and two-platform lifecycle evidence

features.description: Launch the NOLF orchestrator with live game, project tree, editor and preferred agent CLI onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: A documented launch command opens an explicit NOLF project with tree/editor, real terminals and an interactive live NOLF game tab on macOS and Windows.
The standalone Bash launcher finds, installs/downloads, updates or launches the preferred supported CLI agent and supports a custom executable; the real CLI boots in the selected root.
Verify file saves and recovery drafts, session detach/reattach/Stop, tab moves and GUI restart through the actual workflow; record live NOLF and agent evidence alongside automated checks.
features.deliverable: launchable workspace and docs/evidence/nolf-workspace.md

features.description: Define the backend-neutral draw list and the SDL_Renderer reference adapter for the desktop.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned draw-list contract covers clip, rounded alpha rectangles, frames with inner highlight, shadows, text runs in two faces, tinted icons, focus rings and game textures in logical pixels with a density factor; nothing above it includes a graphics-API header.
microui commands and the owned control layer emit only draw-list commands; pinned upstream microui stays unmodified.
The SDL_Renderer adapter consumes the list; native smoke snapshots stay byte-identical to the pre-change baseline while CTest and the native desktop suite pass.
features.deliverable: orchestrator/native/render/ contract and reference adapter with evidence

features.description: Implement the OpenGL adapter on macOS behind the draw list.
acceptance_criteria: An OpenGL core-profile adapter renders every draw-list primitive through owned, versioned shaders with glyph and icon atlases; backend selection is explicit with SDL_Renderer fallback and is recorded in run evidence.
Per-primitive and whole-screen snapshot comparisons against the reference adapter pass within a tolerance recorded before the run on macOS.
Frame time and memory are measured against budgets set beforehand, and the native desktop suite passes on the OpenGL backend.
features.deliverable: OpenGL adapter and docs/evidence per desktop

features.description: Implement the Metal adapter on macOS behind the draw list.
acceptance_criteria: The Metal adapter renders every draw-list primitive with the same snapshot comparisons and measurements as the OpenGL adapter on macOS.
Backend selection, fallback and evidence recording match the OpenGL adapter.
features.deliverable: Metal adapter and docs/evidence

features.description: Implement the Vulkan adapter on Windows, extending to other platforms when they are targeted.
acceptance_criteria: The Vulkan adapter renders every draw-list primitive with the same snapshot comparisons and measurements as the OpenGL adapter on Windows.
Backend selection, fallback and evidence recording match the OpenGL adapter; additional platforms record their own evidence.
features.deliverable: Vulkan adapter and docs/evidence

features.description: Implement the Claude Design foundations on the GPU renderer: theme generation, the owned control layer, toolbar, tab strip and status bar.
acceptance_criteria: design/tokens.css layers and presets generate the runtime theme, and the default, teal and light presets switch live on the GPU backend.

An owned control library over pristine microui provides the design's buttons, selects, fields, checkboxes, sliders, separators, focus ring and transition clock in microui's conventions, as its own build target with no workspace dependencies.

The toolbar, tab strip and status bar match their Claude Design cards on macOS: a generated card reference asserts geometry and resolved colours per state in a native snapshot test, and the full snapshots are recorded as evidence.
Every existing desktop behaviour gate still passes on the GPU backend.
features.deliverable: themed native desktop and docs/evidence

features.description: Make the renderer a curated capability with one game adopting it through an adapter.
acceptance_criteria: A catalog entry carries the library-quality record: contract, pinned dependencies, measured resource behaviour and conformance checks.
One game adopts the renderer through its own adapter with passing integration checks and can revert without workspace changes.
The renderer stays optional for games and curated libraries; no umbrella runtime is required.
features.deliverable: catalog entry, conformance checks and adoption evidence

features.description: Verify the OpenGL adapter on Windows behind the draw list.
acceptance_criteria: The OpenGL adapter builds and starts on the Windows desktop from the authorized source transfer (KI-014), with backend selection and evidence recording as on macOS.
Per-primitive and whole-screen snapshot comparisons against the reference adapter pass on Windows within the tolerances recorded in spec 068.
Frame time and memory are measured on Windows against the spec 068 budgets, and the native desktop suite passes there on the OpenGL backend.
features.deliverable: docs/evidence for the Windows OpenGL adapter

features.description: Register project file formats through a versioned declaration and run their bounded preview commands.
acceptance_criteria: contracts/project-v1.schema.json defines contract 1 (formats with id, title, case-insensitive match globs, modes, default, literal argv preview/entry commands with ${file}/${entry} placeholders and timeoutMs/maxBytes bounds); the service rejects unknown contracts, shell-style argv[0], unknown placeholders, missing keys and non-array commands, and reports a malformed declaration visibly without disabling the root.

Formats, preview (tree/text), entry (size, SHA-256, text when UTF-8 without NUL, hex window) and raw byte-window routes run declared commands only on explicit requests, inside the authenticated root boundary, with cwd = project root, the shell environment, no shell, and fail with stderr's first line on non-zero exit, timeout or oversized output; the host and the replaceable workspace worker both serve them.

The root-bound MCP tool preview_file returns the parsed subtree or text and entry facts through the identical command; service tests exercise host, worker and MCP paths with a temporary project producer, and the nolf-improved declaration with relith-rez is recorded as a real consumer check.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/074-project-format-registry.md, contracts/project-v1.schema.json, orchestrator/server/formats.mjs and its tests

features.description: Open registered formats in the native editor with raw hex and preview modes.
acceptance_criteria: A tab whose file name matches a registered format opens in the declared default mode with a visible switch among its modes; raw is a read-only hex view (offset, 16 bytes per row, ASCII column) over a bounded paged window and is the fallback for every file the text read rejects; the chosen mode survives GUI restart.

Preview shows a collapsible tree with sizes for kind tree and a read-only text pane for kind text; selecting a tree file with an entry command shows its bytes read-only as text or hex; a failing command shows stderr's first line, names the command and offers Retry; Save and drafts stay text-only.

A native fixture drives open, mode switching, tree expansion, entry selection, restart, failure and unregistered-binary fallback through real SDL events; the owner verifies nolf/NOLF.REZ in the real project window after a layered update.
features.deliverable: orchestrator/native/formatview.c, hexview.c, native-format-registry.spec.mjs and evidence

features.description: Declare a project dashboard (contract 2) and serve its actions, availability and captures.
acceptance_criteria: contracts/project-v1.schema.json accepts contract 1 and 2; contract 2 adds an optional dashboard of groups and actions (kind script, log or capture with their fields, requires/tools/artifacts) with unknown keys, unknown kinds, mixed-kind fields, duplicate ids, non-root-relative paths and bad env keys rejected by name, structural errors before cross rules; a bad dashboard is reported without disabling the formats section; the copied nolf-improved merged document validates with zero errors.

The dashboard route computes per-action availability (missing required files inside the root boundary, tools absent from the sidecar PATH) without running anything; dashboard-run creates the retained script or log session with literal args and env merged over the shell environment and refuses unavailable actions; dashboard-capture runs the command once under contract-1 bounds, requires the PNG signature, writes <into>/<timestamp>.png and appends to manifest.json inside the root, rejecting non-PNG output and escaping directories.

Host and replaceable worker serve the routes; MCP dashboard_actions lists availability read-only, dashboard_capture returns the manifest entry, open_script accepts env; service tests fail before the reader knows contract 2 and cover every rule above.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/075-project-dashboard.md, contracts/project-v1.schema.json (contract 2), orchestrator/server/dashboard.mjs and tests

features.description: Render the project dashboard as a native tab with runnable actions.
acceptance_criteria: A Dashboard tab per declared root opens from the toolbar and automatically once when a bound root declares a dashboard and the layout holds none; groups are sections, each available action is a button with its title and description, an unavailable action is a label naming the first missing item.

A script action opens its retained session as a script tab with its args and env, a log action opens a terminal tab, a capture action runs the capture and shows the written path in the status line, artifacts reveal their path in the project tree, and a declaration error renders in the tab without disabling the workspace.

A native fixture drives auto-open, groups, the disabled action, the script tab output, the capture file and manifest, artifact reveal, close, restart and toolbar reopen through real SDL events; the owner verifies the real nolf-improved dashboard after its staged section moves into project.json and a layered update.
features.deliverable: orchestrator/native/dashboard.c, native-dashboard.spec.mjs and evidence

features.description: Implement the Claude Design update for the tree, editor, terminal and session browser.
acceptance_criteria: The tree, editor, terminal and session browser match their Claude Design cards on macOS under the generated card reference, including the editor breadcrumb bar, gutter, current-line tint and syntax colours, the terminal cell metrics, and the session table's state pills.
Overlay scrollbars with rounded thumbs replace the current bars in every scrollable view, with rest, hover and dragging states.
Every existing desktop behaviour gate still passes on the GPU backend.
features.deliverable: themed views and docs/evidence

features.description: Implement the Claude Design menus, theme panel and theme files.
acceptance_criteria: Menus and popovers match their cards on macOS as one overlay layer with a shadow, keyboard hints and separators.
The theme panel matches its card, including the accent hue slider drawn with the draw-list gradient primitive.

Theme files in the card's format override all three token layers, import and export from the theme panel, and a project root's theme is offered and applied only on explicit activation, remembered per root.
Every existing desktop behaviour gate still passes on the GPU backend.
features.deliverable: themed overlays, theme files and docs/evidence

features.description: Record Windows card evidence for the Claude Design update.
acceptance_criteria: The card reference assertions for every surface covered by F60, F67 and F68 pass on the Windows desktop.
Native snapshots of those surfaces on Windows are recorded as evidence alongside the macOS set.
features.deliverable: docs/evidence for the Windows design update

features.description: Store the project integration recipe as a runbook, a scaffolding wizard, copied templates and a test.
acceptance_criteria: docs/runbooks/project-integration.md carries the ordered recipe with runnable commands (prerequisites, submodule pin policy, editor.sh launching point, contract-3 .rengine/project.json, the tests a consumer keeps and how to register them, skills/AGENTS wiring, the cross-vendor review gate, opening the project window, layered updates, owner-verified consumer gates, pin bumps), the nolf-improved and vtmb-vr instances as tables, and what the orchestrator UI will automate.

orchestrator/actions/integrate-project.sh follows the lib/wizard.sh conventions and scaffolds a consumer in five stages (verify the repository and the advertised pin, pin third_party/rengine, install editor.sh, write .rengine/project.json, copy the declaration test); explicit arguments run unattended, missing values prompt only on a TTY, existing files are reported and skipped, --dry-run prints the plan and writes nothing, and the follow-ups it leaves to the project are printed.

orchestrator/templates/project/ holds editor.sh, the reference project.json, the generic test_rengine_project_decl.py and a README naming each destination, none of them naming a specific game or format; orchestrator/tests/integrate-project.test.mjs scaffolds a temporary git repository and asserts the declared structure through the shipped schema and cross-rule modules, the contract-1 core through readDeclaration, the launcher dry runs, the copied Python test, skip-never-overwrite, an empty --dry-run and the pinned submodule.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/077-project-integration-recipe.md, docs/runbooks/project-integration.md, orchestrator/actions/integrate-project.sh, orchestrator/templates/project/ and orchestrator/tests/integrate-project.test.mjs

features.description: Declare a project's games in .rengine/project.json (contract 3, games array) and launch any of them from the dashboard, the launcher and generic agent tools.
acceptance_criteria: contracts/project-v1.schema.json accepts contracts 1 and 2 unchanged and contract 3 with an optional games array (1-16 records of id, title, executable candidates, literal args, env, cwd, requires, surface embedded or external) beside the optional dashboard of spec 075; declaring games requires contract 3, so an older reader answers unknown contract rather than unknown key; a bad games array is reported as gamesError by name without disabling the formats or the dashboard; duplicate ids, a 17th record, bad or reserved env keys, placeholders in args, more than 8 executables, unknown surfaces and keys, shell argv[0] and escaping requires/cwd paths are rejected.

game-config and game_preflight take an optional gameId (default: the first declared game; an unknown id names the declared ids) and report declared, title, surface, the first resolvable executable, args, env, cwd, requires, named issues (undeclared root, malformed declaration, missing candidates, each missing required file, a missing cwd, surface prerequisites) and ready without running anything; game, launch_game, the toolbar control and --launch-game reuse the running session of that root AND game id, or spawn it with the declared cwd and env, reserving a surface only for embedded; the session carries title <title> · <root name>, surface and game, and one root can run several declared games at once.

No specific game is named in server, native, agent, theme or package-script code and no nolf_* tool alias remains; an external game tab shows the retained output with a running/exited status row; service tests and a native fixture drive all of the above; the real-NOLF qualification runs through a written contract-3 declaration; the owner verifies the real consumers after a layered workspace/desktop/connector update. (Corrected 2026-09-06 by owner decision, recorded in spec 078 and Codex-progress session 27: the toolbar game control this criterion originally required — absent without games, a title button for one, a Games menu for several — was built in 0cf70b6 and then removed outright, because dashboard launches reached only a terminal tab. Launching moved to the dashboard game action of F72; a configurable toolbar is a later, separately scoped feature.)
features.deliverable: docs/specs/078-project-game-declaration.md, contracts/project-v1.schema.json (games), orchestrator/server/games.mjs and game-rules.mjs, mcp-worker game tools, external game view, games.test.mjs, contracts.test.mjs, native-game-declaration.spec.mjs and evidence

features.description: Launch a declared game from the project dashboard through an action kind game, and remove the toolbar game control.
acceptance_criteria: contracts/project-v1.schema.json adds the dashboard action kind game with a required game key (the id of a record in the same declaration's contract-3 games array) and an optional literal args list appended to that record's own args; the reader rejects a game action without game, one carrying another kind's field, a ${...} placeholder in its args and a reference to an undeclared id (naming the id and the declared ids) as dashboardError, leaving the formats and the games array intact, and skips the reference check when gamesError is already set.

GET /api/dashboard marks a game action available from its referenced record's preflight (the spec-078 path, not a second copy of the checks) and unavailable with that record's first issue when the executable is missing, in addition to the action's own requires and tools; POST /api/dashboard-run on a game action returns a type game session carrying the record's args followed by the action's, reuses it on a second run, and refuses a second action referencing the same record with different args with status 409 naming both argv; the replaceable worker serves the same through the retained host's game route.

The toolbar game button, its Games menu, its unavailable-entry rendering, its per-game preflight cache and its theme metrics and strings are gone; toolbar row one is a fixed set of columns whose arithmetic no longer depends on the declaration; design.py check passes; a native fixture shows no toolbar game control for a root that declares games, launches an external game from a dashboard game action into its tab with the running status, reuses it on a second click and shows an unbuilt record's action as a disabled label naming its first issue; RENGINE_NOLF_ROOT=... npm run test:game-nolf launches the real NOLF build through a dashboard game action and sees its frames.

Because a section fails whole and the dashboard is now the only human path to a launch, every cross-rule error in the declaration names the offending record beside its JSON path in all three sections ($.dashboard.groups[1].actions[1] (quest-screen).into must be root-relative, $.games[1] (vtmb-vr).cwd ..., $.formats[0] (troika-vpk).default ...); an action with no usable id is placed by its group, a record with no named ancestor keeps the bare path and undefined is never printed; duplicate-id errors keep the bare path so the repeating occurrence stays unambiguous; the report stays capped at three problems and names how many it hides; the native status row carries the id early enough not to clip it.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/078-project-game-declaration.md and 075-project-dashboard.md, contracts/project-v1.schema.json (game action kind), orchestrator/server/dashboard-rules.mjs, dashboard.mjs, games.mjs and sessions.mjs, orchestrator/runtime/worker.mjs, native dashboard tab and toolbar removal, theme.json/theme.h, dashboard.test.mjs, contracts.test.mjs, native-game-declaration.spec.mjs, native-nolf.spec.mjs and evidence

features.description: Serve the declaration-backed game preflight from the replaceable workspace worker, so a routine layered update delivers the per-project game capability.
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator/server/games.mjs exports inspectGame(root, gameId) — the single body Games.inspect delegates to — and orchestrator/runtime/worker.mjs serves GET /api/game-config from it, so the dashboard's game-action availability and game_preflight both answer from the project's own declaration above a retained session host that predates contract 3; the worker advertises projectGame: 1 beside dashboard: 1 and a layered workspace update alone lights the MCP guard up.

Launching stays with the session host, which owns Sessions (PTY), the embedded Surfaces reservation and the session-id map behind /surface, and whose /api/terminal refuses type game; the worker advertises projectGameLaunch only by mirroring the host's own projectGame, refuses POST /api/game and the game branch of /api/dashboard-run by name above an older host instead of forwarding into the removed built-in game, and launch_game gates on projectGameLaunch with that message. supervisor.mjs claims neither capability in its workspaceWorkerUnavailable fallback, where the host answers.

A regression drives a worker above a proxy that advertises only handoff: 1 and answers game-config with the removed built-in NOLF config: it asserts capabilities.projectGame is 1 and projectGameLaunch absent, that game-config returns each declared record (including an unknown gameId 404 naming the declared ids), that the dashboard marks a declared game available, that both launch paths and launch_game refuse by name, and that game_preflight through the real MCP connector answers from the declaration; the merged-host path keeps projectGameLaunch: 1 and launches through the worker's game route unchanged. npm test, npm run test:desktop, CTest, ./init.sh, design.py check, features.py validate and RENGINE_NOLF_ROOT=... npm run test:game-nolf pass, and both live consumer declarations re-validate through the fixed code. Passing waits on the owner's live verification after update_workspace, as F71/F72 do.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/078-project-game-declaration.md (layered-update asymmetry), orchestrator/server/games.mjs and main.mjs, orchestrator/runtime/worker.mjs, orchestrator/agents/mcp-worker.mjs, orchestrator/tests/games.test.mjs and dashboard.test.mjs
